title: Burger joint wins ruling in dispute over UFO-themed mural
excerpt: The 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals found that Salina, Kan., violated the First Amendment.
content:
Home » News » Burger joint wins ruling in dispute over UFO-themed mural

By the Free Speech Center, published on November 12, 2026

Photo courtesy flickr

The 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals has sided with the Cozy Inn, a burger restaurant in Salina, Kan., in its dispute with the city over a mural depicting UFOs as hamburgers, Kansas Public Radio reported.

“Steve Howard, owner of the Cozy Inn, filed the lawsuit in early 2024 after Salina officials told him to stop painting the mural,” Kansas Public Radio said. “Salina considered the artwork a regulated sign instead of an unregulated mural, saying that the depicted UFOs looked too much like hamburgers, the Cozy’s signature item.”

The 10th Circuit said Salina had violated the First Amendment because it “failed to justify the distinction between regulated signs and unregulated murals. It did not show that signs pose greater danger to Salina’s interest in safety, aesthetic, and property values.”
